question: Marriage, divorce and remarriage: what was allowed?

answers.label: Separation for adultery is allowed, but no remarriage while the spouse lives
The innocent party may divorce and remarry

overview.text: The earliest writers allow separation for adultery but not remarriage: Hermas says the husband must stay single so his wife can return if she repents. Justin and Athenagoras count remarriage after divorce as adultery.
Augustine held the bond lasts until death, and the Latin West made this law (Trent, 1563), while carefully not condemning the Greek practice.
The Orthodox allow a second marriage in some cases as a concession, and the Reformed allow the innocent party to remarry after adultery or desertion.

quotes.author: Shepherd of Hermas
quotes.english: "Sir," I said, "if a man has a wife who believes in the Lord, and he finds her in adultery, does the husband sin if he lives with her?" "As long as he does not know," he said, "he does not sin. But if the husband knows her sin and the wife does not repent but continues in her fornication, and the husband lives with her, he becomes guilty of her sin." "What then shall the husband do, sir?" "Let him put her away, and let the husband remain by himself. But if, having put away his wife, he marries another, he too commits adultery." "And if, sir, after she is put away the wife repents and wants to return to her husband, shall she not be received?" "Indeed, if the husband does not receive her, he sins."
quotes.original: Κύριε, φημί, εἰ γυναῖκα ἔχῃ τις πιστὴν ἐν κυρίῳ καὶ ταύτην εὕρῃ ἐν μοιχείᾳ τινί, ἆρα ἁμαρτάνει ὁ ἀνὴρ συνζῶν μετ’ αὐτῆς; Ἄχρι τῆς ἀγνοίας, φησίν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει: ἐὰν δὲ γνῷ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν αὐτῆς καὶ μὴ μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνή, ἀλλ’ ἐπιμένῃ τῇ πορνείᾳ αὐτῆς καὶ συνζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ μετ’ αὐτῆς, ἔνοχος γίνεται τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῆς ... Ἀπολυσάτω, φησίν, αὐτὴν καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐφ̓ ἑαυτῷ μενέτω: ἐὰν δὲ ἀπολύσας τὴν γυναῖκα ἑτέραν γαμήσῃ, καὶ αὐτὸς μοιχᾶται. Ἐὰν οὖν, φημί, κύριε, μετὰ τὸ ἀπολυθῆναι τὴν γυναῖκα μετανοήσῃ ἡ γυνὴ καὶ θελήσῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτῆς ἄνδρα ὑποστρέψαι, οὐ παραδεχθήσεται; Καὶ μήν, φησίν, ἐὰν μὴ παραδέξηται αὐτὴν ὁ ἀνήρ, ἁμαρτάνει
quotes.context: Separation for adultery is allowed, but not remarriage, so that the door to repentance stays open. Hermas says the same applies to a wife.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: Just as those who make second marriages by human law are sinners in the eyes of our Teacher, so are those who look at a woman to lust after her.
quotes.original: Ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ νόμῳ ἀνθρωπίνῳ διγαμίας ποιούμενοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ τῷ· ἡμετέρῳ διδασκάλῳ εἰσί, καὶ οἱ προσβλέποντες γυναικὶ πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς
quotes.context: "Second marriages" here probably means remarriage after divorce, which Roman law allowed.

quotes.author: Athenagoras
quotes.english: ... either to remain as one was born, or in one marriage; for a second marriage is a decent adultery. "Whoever puts away his wife," he says, "and marries another, commits adultery": he does not allow a man to put away the woman whose virginity he ended, nor to marry again. For whoever deprives himself of his first wife, even if she has died, is an adulterer in disguise.
quotes.original: ἢ οἷός τις ἐτέχθη μένειν ἢ ἐφ᾿ ἑνὶ γάμῳ· ὁ γὰρ δεύτερος εὐπρεπής ἐστι μοιχεία. Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἀπολύσῃ, φησί, τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην, μοιχᾶται, οὔτε ἀπολύειν ἐπιτρέπων ἧς ἔπαυσέ τις τὴν παρθενίαν οὔτε ἐπιγαμεῖν. Ὁ γὰρ ἀποστερῶν ἑαυτὸν τῆς προτέρας γυναικός, καὶ εἰ τέθνηκε, μοιχός ἐστι παρακεκαλυμμένος
quotes.context: Athenagoras goes further than most: even remarriage after a spouse's death. The Church did not adopt this; it allowed widows and widowers to remarry.

quotes.author: Origen of Alexandria
quotes.english: But now too, contrary to what is written, some of the rulers of the church have permitted a woman to marry while her husband is living... 'A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives'... and a woman married to another man while her husband lives 'will be called an adulteress'.
quotes.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ νῦν παρὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον τινὲς καὶ τῶν προεστώτων τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐπέτρεψαν γαμεῖν γυναικὶ ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρός ... Δέδεται γυνὴ ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς ... ἡ γαμηθεῖσα ἑτέρῳ ἀνδρὶ ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς μοιχαλὶς χρηματίσει
quotes.context: Origen reports the concession; he does not praise it. He adds that it was 'not altogether without reason', granted 'in comparison with greater evils', against what was ordained from the beginning. That sentence is too broken in the PG 13 scan to quote word for word, so it is reported here rather than quoted. The Greek witness named for this gap in the store (Khazarzar PG 11-17) in fact contains only Books 10 and 11 of the commentary, so the words quoted are read from the PG 13 scan text (poor OCR, columns interleaved), saved as a witness in Wave 3.

quotes.author: Basil of Caesarea
quotes.english: The Lord's ruling, followed through in its sense, fits men and women equally: no one may leave a marriage except for unchastity. But custom does not run that way. For women we find much strictness. ... Custom also orders wives to keep husbands who are adulterers and live in fornication. So a wife who leaves her husband and goes to another man is an adulteress; but the husband who was left is pardonable, and a woman who lives with such a man is not condemned.
quotes.original: Ἡ δὲ τοῦ Κυρίου ἀπόφασις κατὰ μὲν τὴν τῆς ἐννοίας ἀκολουθίαν ἐξ ἴσου καὶ ἀνδράσι καὶ γυναιξὶν ἁρμόζει περὶ τοῦ μὴ ἐξεῖναι γάμου ἐξίστασθαι παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας. ... Ἡ δὲ συνήθεια οὐχ οὕτως ἔχει. Ἡ δὲ συνήθεια καὶ μοιχεύοντας ἄνδρας καὶ ἐν πορνείαις ὄντας κατέχεσθαι ὑπὸ γυναικῶν προστάσσει. ... Ὥστε ἡ καταλιποῦσα μοιχαλίς ἐστιν, εἰ ἐπ’ ἄλλον ἦλθεν ἄνδρα. ὁ δὲ καταλειφθεὶς συγγνωστός ἐστι, καὶ ἡ συνοικοῦσα τῷ τοιούτῳ οὐ κατακρίνεται.
quotes.context: Basil states the Lord's rule as equal for both sexes, then records that church custom (synetheia) held wives to a stricter account than husbands, and let a deserted husband's new union pass without condemnation. A canon of discipline describing practice, and an early root of the East's more lenient custom. Quoted from the PG 32 scan (poor OCR).

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.english: Because of so great an evil, a man may not put away his wife except for the cause of fornication. For then he does not make her an adulteress by putting her away, but puts away an adulteress.
quotes.original: Propter hoc ergo tam magnum malum non licet homini dimittere uxorem nisi ex causa fornicationis. tunc enim non ipse dimittendo facit adulteram, sed dimittit adulteram.
quotes.context: Augustine argues that even after such a separation neither may remarry while the other lives.

quotes.author: Council of Trent
quotes.english: If anyone says that the Church errs when she has taught and teaches, according to the teaching of the Gospel and the apostles, that the bond of marriage cannot be dissolved because of the adultery of one of the spouses, and that neither, not even the innocent one who gave no cause for adultery, can contract another marriage while the other spouse lives ... let him be anathema.
quotes.original: Si quis dixerit, Ecclesiam errare, cum docuit et docet, iuxta evangelicam et apostolicam doctrinam propter adulterium alterius coniugum matrimonii vinculum non posse dissolvi, et utrumque, vel etiam innocentem, qui causam adulterio non dedit, non posse, altero coniuge vivente, aliud matrimonium contrahere
quotes.context: Worded carefully so as not to condemn the Greek churches, which allowed remarriage after adultery.

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: In the case of adultery after marriage, it is lawful for the innocent party to sue out a divorce: and, after the divorce, to marry another, as if the offending party were dead. ... nothing but adultery, or such willful desertion as can no way be remedied by the church, or civil magistrate, is cause sufficient of dissolving the bond of marriage.
quotes.original: In the case of adultery after marriage, it is lawful for the innocent party to sue out a divorce: and, after the divorce, to marry another, as if the offending party were dead. 6. Although the corruption of man be such as is apt to study arguments unduly to put asunder those whom God hath joined together in marriage: yet, nothing but adultery, or such willful desertion as can no way be remedied by the church, or civil magistrate, is cause sufficient of dissolving the bond of marriage
quotes.context: The Reformed view, close to the Orthodox practice of allowing remarriage in some cases.

gaps.author: Council of Carthage
gaps.why: Neither divorced spouse may remarry; an imperial law should be sought. Still not quoted: no verifiable text on the mini. Tried in Wave 3 (Oct 2026): the Bruns witness file in the store is a 401 error page (165 bytes), and the archive.org Bruns item itself returns 401; the library's Carthage 419 book (PL 56 Italian form) does not contain this canon (searched dimissus, coniungantur, reconcilientur: absent; its canon 102 concerns widows on the church's stipend); Munier's CCSL 149 text is copyrighted.
gaps.source_hint: Bruns (1839), vol. 1, African code; needs an open scan of Bruns or of PL 56/67
